text.p: Italian bank Banco Ambrosiano Veneto (Ambroveneto) will make a capital issue of "major dimensions" by the end of this year, chairman Giovanni Bazoli told a news conference on Tuesday.
Ambroveneto has said before it intends to increase its capital increase but has given no indication of size.
Bazoli said there were two possibilities for the operation, one being an increase without defining precisely what the funds would be used for, or one with a definite goal in view.
Bazoli said in February the banking group planned to make a capital increase this year but that it would be made within the context of a specific industrial plan.
Bazoli said on Tuesday Ambroveneto was convinced it must increase its dimensions in order to follow through initiatives it was carrying out.

Growth could come in two ways, Bazoli said, with the first "a large-scale combining with institutions equal or bigger in dimension to ours. This will depend on internal and external circumstances and will also depend on the agreement of our shareholders."
"Above all if it regards a privatisation it will require a lot of investment," he said.
The second possibility would be "to increase size with internal growth, by acquisitions or agreements with banks equal to or smaller than us," he said.
In that case he had the support of shareholders, Bazoli said, denying there had been requests from shareholders to leave the shareholder pact.
Bazoli made no mention of savings bank Cariplo, which newspapers here have reported as seeking a strategic link-up with Ambroveneto.
